display.purpose: Landing hero only. One per page.

headline.purpose: Landing section headings. The only place fluid clamp sizing is correct.

title.purpose: Console pane headings. Fixed, never fluid.

body.purpose: Default copy. Prose holds a 65-75ch measure.

label.purpose: Table headers, metric keys, pills, stage chips, rail groups. 11px floor.

code.purpose: Mutation notation, accessions, job IDs, worker names, event log. Never prose.

shadows.name: state-ring
shadows.purpose: The only box-shadow in the console. A second hairline reinforcing a live round's blue border. Zero offset, zero blur: a ring, not an elevation.

shadows.name: deck-glow
shadows.purpose: Presentation and marketing surfaces ONLY. Never in product UI, where a coloured halo is decoration competing with the one live signal. Still cyan: the deck has not been brought onto the blue palette yet.

shadows.name: deck-drop
shadows.purpose: Presentation surfaces only. Lifts deck cards off the ground plane.

motion.name: duration-state
motion.purpose: Button background and border-color transitions. Users are in a task; nothing waits on choreography.

motion.name: pulse-live
motion.purpose: The single authored moment: the dot on a running status pill. Suppressed under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Button :active. The only positional feedback in the system.

typeScale.name: --t-xs
typeScale.purpose: Labels, chips, pills, table headers. The floor.

radii.name: --r-chip
radii.purpose: Stage chips — read as a strip, not pressed.

radii.name: --r-sm
radii.purpose: Controls: buttons, inputs, residue chips, nav items.

fluidSteps.name: display
fluidSteps.purpose: Landing hero only, one per page.

extensions.fluidStepNote: Fluid steps interpolate BETWEEN scale steps, so their clamp() endpoints are deliberately not scale tokens: 1rem, 2.75rem and 4.125rem exist only as the ends of a range. Fluid type is confined to the landing page; nothing in the console uses it. A detector reading only the frontmatter roles will flag these endpoints.

spacingScale.name: --sp-xs
spacingScale.purpose: Tightest grouping: label to its value.

spacingScale.purpose: The work grid gap; separating blocks.

narrative.overview:
The obvious thing is obvious. Whatever the user came to do — read a campaign's state, confirm which residues the planner may touch, decide what goes to the bench — sits in front, uncluttered, at full contrast. Nothing competes with it for attention. The surface is quiet enough that a single blue element reads as *the* live thing on the screen.

Underneath that clean surface, every decision is accounted for and nothing is hidden. The ledger shows refusals next to approvals. The benchmark shows the held-out correlation next to the enrichment. A round that was priced too high and rejected stays on screen as a card of its own. This is not decoration or humility theatre: it is the product's actual claim, so the visual system has to make the record inspectable rather than tuck it behind a disclosure.

The register is precise, sober and unembellished. Density is earned, never performed — tables run dense because a scientist is comparing rows, while prose stays at a readable measure. Accent colour is scarce and always means something. The world is deliberately single-theme dark and will not be given a light mode.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black blue ground (#070a12) with a four-step tonal surface ramp instead of shadows
One scarce blue accent reserved for live state, current selection and primary action
Outfit for display and labels, Inter for body, Fira Code only for code, data and measurement
Semantic colour vocabulary that is stable across every surface: blue running, emerald complete, amber waiting, rose refused, neutral idle
Evidence stays visible — refusals, limits and negative results are designed for, not hidden

rules.name: The One Live Thing Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue marks what is happening now. If a screen shows two different blue elements claiming liveness, one of them is wrong. Current selection and primary action may also carry it, but a screen with blue on more than roughly a tenth of its area has lost the signal.

rules.name: The Stable Meaning Rule
rules.body: A colour means the same thing on every surface. Emerald is never 'a nice green for a heading'; rose is never 'an attention grabber'. If a new state needs a colour and none of the five fits, the state is probably neutral.

rules.name: The Tinted Text Rule
rules.body: Any accent text sitting on its own tint must be contrast-checked against the composited background, not against the tint value. Two of the five accents needed a lighter step to clear AA; assume the next one will too.

rules.name: The Eleven Pixel Floor
rules.body: No text below 11px, and tracked uppercase especially. Labels were lifted off 9.5px and 10px because tracked caps at that size stop being readable and start being texture.

rules.name: The Mono Means Data Rule
rules.body: Fira Code marks code, identifiers, measurements and tabular figures. It is never a costume for 'technical'. Prose in a monospace face is a bug.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number that sits in a column or changes in place carries font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. Costs, fitness values, counts and timestamps must not jitter as they update.

rules.name: The Shrinkable Item Rule
rules.body: Every grid or flex item that can contain a table carries min-width: 0. A grid item defaults to min-width: auto, which sizes it to the min-content of its widest nowrap table and drags the whole page into horizontal scroll. An overflow-x: auto wrapper cannot save a parent that refuses to shrink.

rules.name: The Sticky Clearance Rule
rules.body: The prototype bar is sticky, so html carries scroll-padding-top: 64px. Any in-page scroll target — an anchor, a pane switch calling scrollIntoView — must clear fixed chrome, or it lands underneath it.

rules.name: The No Horizontal Scroll Rule
rules.body: The page holds at 360px with no horizontal overflow. Wide tables scroll inside their own wrapper; the document never does.

rules.name: The Tonal-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Product UI conveys depth by surface step and hairline. If a console element needs a shadow to read as separate, the real problem is that it is on the wrong surface step.

rules.name: The Deck-Only Glow Rule
rules.body: Accent halos belong to the deck. A zero-offset coloured glow in the console is decoration, and the console has no decoration budget.

rules.name: The No Accent Rail Rule
rules.body: No coloured border-left or border-right above 1px on cards, list items or callouts. Accent rails were removed from stats and the honest-limits callout deliberately; state belongs in the figure's own colour, not in a stripe beside it.

rules.name: The Dashed Means Provisional Rule
rules.body: A dashed border is reserved for the not-yet and the set-aside. A solid border is a committed thing.

rules.name: The No Literal Sizes Rule
rules.body: Every font-size is a scale token. A new size is a decision about the scale, made in DESIGN.md first — the page once carried 21 distinct sizes for nine roles, which is how a scale rots.

rules.name: The Reader’s Base Size Rule
rules.body: The scale is in rem and nothing sets html { font-size }, so a reader who raises their browser default gets a bigger page. Layout must survive it: every row that can run out of space wraps. Verified at 200% text on a 400px viewport with no horizontal overflow.

rules.name: The Fluid Endpoints Rule
rules.body: Only the landing page uses fluid type, and a fluid step’s clamp() endpoints are not scale tokens — they are the ends of a range. Console type is fixed, because a heading that shrinks inside a narrow work area looks broken rather than responsive.

rules.name: The One Spacing Scale Rule
rules.body: Margins and gaps come from the six --sp tokens. The markup once carried ten different inline margin values against a grid with its own 22px gap, which is two spacing systems competing; a value off the scale is a decision about the scale, made in DESIGN.md first.

rules.name: The Binding Limit Rule
rules.body: Where the user sets several limits at once, the interface names which one actually bites. A budget field alone makes spend a number to type; saying the round cap stops you first, or that the ledger would refuse the first round, makes it a consequence to read.

rules.name: The Capped ViewBox Rule
rules.body: An SVG chart caps its width, because the viewBox scales its text with it. Uncapped in a wide column a 10px axis label renders at 22px, which is how a chart stops looking like part of the interface.

rules.name: The Category Is Not A State Rule
rules.body: Structural annotations borrow shape, size or position rather than a status hue. The residue track marks catalytic positions by height because the five status colours each already mean one thing, and a sixth meaning for amber would cost more than it bought.

dos: Do keep Signal Blue scarce. One live thing per screen; primary action and current selection may share it, but roughly a tenth of the screen is the ceiling.
Do convey depth with the surface ramp and 1px hairlines, never with a shadow, in product UI.
Do check accent text against the composited background. #f43f5e on rgba(244,63,94,0.12) over the card is 4.11:1, not the ratio the raw values suggest.
Do give every grid or flex item that may contain a table min-width: 0.
Do use tabular-nums on every figure in a column or one that updates in place.
Do set scroll-padding-top to clear the sticky bar on any in-page scroll target.
Do show refusals, limits and negative results at full contrast. The ledger's refused rows and the benchmark's held-out correlation are designed for, not disclosed away.
Do keep tracked uppercase labels at 11px or above.
Do theme the surfaces the browser draws — selection, caret, accent-color, scrollbars. Default light scrollbars on a near-black page are the giveaway that nobody looked.
Do keep every font-size, radius and tint on a token. The five one-off hexes and sixteen rgba literals that used to sit in the stylesheet are what made the accent drift to seven different alphas.
donts: Don't add a light theme or a theme toggle. The dark-only commitment is intentional and binding.
Don't reach for gradient text, neon halos, glass or blur as decoration, or animated mesh backgrounds. Confirmed anti-reference.
Don't soften the product into consumer-SaaS friendliness — pastel rounding, illustrations, mascots, emoji as iconography, chirpy microcopy. Confirmed anti-reference.
Don't wear monospace as a costume. Fira Code is for code, identifiers, data and measurement; no CRT scanlines, no ASCII chrome. Confirmed anti-reference.
Don't put a kicker or eyebrow above a heading. A standalone label that is the heading of a card is fine; a tracked-caps line stacked on top of an h2 is not, and these were removed deliberately.
Don't give a card a coloured accent rail above 1px.
Don't de-emphasise with opacity on anything containing text. An excluded cluster was at 0.45 and became unreadable — move it to the Panel surface and keep its text legible instead.
Don't use fluid clamp() type in the console. Fluid sizing belongs to the landing page; a console heading that shrinks in a narrow work area looks broken.
Don't let a status colour drift from its meaning, and don't give Analytic Violet a state meaning — it exists only to separate a third figure.
Don't add motion that doesn't carry state. The pulsing dot on a running pill is the one authored moment, and it honours prefers-reduced-motion.
